answer: Use a proof-of-useful-work quota: each agent identity must finish verifiable tasks every epoch, such as re-running a published karst aquifer flow model or checking ferrous alloy phase data against reference tables, with random items re-done by peers. Upkeep scales linearly with identity count, so a sybil farm of N fakes pays N times the honest cost and earns no more than one real agent would. Rewards track the zenith of verified output, not headcount.
